newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close sharply higher on funds, wheat.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close sharply higher on funds, wheat.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended sharply higher with the May contract posting double-digit gains on heavy fund buying ahead of Wednesday's USDA supply and demand report, traders said.

Soybeans also drew strength from a late rally in wheat tied to news Canadian wheat shipments may be hurt by a rail shipping delay that has kept more than 1.5 million tonnes of grain from reaching Pacific ports since January.
Traders said stops were hit above $7.41 per bushel in the March soybean contract. Technical traders had pegged $7.42 as the first resistance point.
"We had strength because of fund buying and once we got over $7.41 we hit stops," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
Traders said they expect USDA will raise its estimates for Argentine and Brazilian soybean production but cut U.S. ending stocks in Wednesday's supply and demand report.

The market reacted quietly to several hints at what Wednesday's supply and demand report will show. The USDA agricultural attache in Argentina raised projections for soybean production to 13.5 million tonnes from 13.0 million.
Soybeans closed three to 10 cents per bushel higher with March up 9-3/4 at $7.49-3/4.
In late trade, Rosenthal Collins bought three million bushels March, traders said.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 35,000 contracts, compared with Monday's actual volume of 28,213 contracts.
